attribution.note: Marcus's own words on his Substack, assessing his own earlier Politico prediction; the quoted tweet is not part of the claim.

semantics.note: Normalisation keeps 'I think we can count', 'largely correct', and the conceded timing miss. It is a qualified retrospective self-assessment of vindication, not a fresh forecast.

contract.note: Contract correctly finds no standard for 'largely correct' and no measure of 'largest'. Choosing one (victims, orgs, damage) would add criteria he did not supply. Declining to set support or contradiction conditions is fair.

evidence.note: Netskope report, available 2026-11-17, before the evaluation date. Describes the third-party snippet compromise reaching 178 brands, but gives no historical ranking and no basis for judging partial vindication.

reviews.rationale: This is Marcus's hedged self-assessment that his prediction was 'largely correct', and he concedes he got the year wrong. With no defined measure of 'largest' and no tolerance for 'largely', no reproducible test exists. The only evidence (e1) gives incident context, not a historical rank, so it cannot settle the claim either way.
